units.translation: 1286. χρίμψε: came near. Lg(P)
1288. νήριτα: the great and countless things. Lg (P)
1290a. κευθμῶνος: of a hollow. Lg (P)
8 -ώματος in (P) : -ωμάτων in L
b. 〈ἵνα τέ σφισιν ἔσκε〉 βόαυλα: where their cattle-stall was. Lg (P)
1291. He says the cattle-stall was filled with smoke from the exhalation of fire from the bulls' mouths.
1299. ἐυρρίνοις: with good hides and well-covered with skins. Or with good breathing; for breath is sent through the nose.
13 ἐρρινωμένοις in (P) : ἐρριμένοις in L : ἐρρινημένοις in AF
1300. μαρμαίρουσι: properly †καίουσι†, but he has transferred the word.
16 1301. Etymologicum Genuinum (B) πιμπράσαι: to blow. III 1301. Apollonius.
15 πιμπράσαι κυρίως καίουσαι proposed by Wil. ad l.
1302-03. 〈ἐξ αὐτοῦ πέλεται βρόμος:〉 from the very violent blowing acting from within.
16 Fr. separated this scholium from the preceding one. ἐπὶ instead of ἀπὸ in K
1304. αἶθος: fire, flame. LgP
1310a. σφῆλε γνύξ: caused to stumble and brought him to his knees.
19 ἐπὶ τὰ γόνατα in LmSmP (here with the reading ὀκλάξ from v. 1308)
b. βεβολημένον: struck and wounded. LgP
1313a. 〈γούνασιν:〉 their own. Lm

b. ἐλυσθείς: stretched out. LGgSmP
1317. 〈ἐνέδησε:〉 with the straps. LgSm (P)
1318a. θοή: because it ends in a sharp sound. Lg (P)
b. κορώνῃ: he fitted it to the ring of the yoke. LGmSm(P)
26 συνήρμοσεν in L (P) : omitted in GS
1319-20. The Tyndaridae, he says, separated themselves from the fire to the ship. Lm (P)
1321a. 〈γέντο:〉 took. Sm
b. θοῶν: sharp. Lg (P)
c. 〈ἔμπλειον:〉 full. Lg
1323a. ἐργατίνης: worker, farmer. LgP

b. ἀκαίνῃ: instead of κέντρῳ. ἄκαινα is a measure of ten feet, an invention of the Thessalians, or a shepherd's staff discovered among the Pelasgians; concerning which Callimachus says (fg 214 Schn. = 7, 7 Pfeiffer): 'both, a goad for oxen and a measure of the field.'
